# ast-grep(sg) ast-grep(sg) is a CLI tool for code structural search, lint, and rewriting. ## What is ast-grep? ast-grep is an [abstract syntax tree](https://dev.to/balapriya/abstract-syntax-tree-ast-explained-in-plain-english-1h38) based tool to search code by pattern code. Think of it as your old-friend [`grep`](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grep), but matching AST nodes instead of text. You can write patterns as if you are writing ordinary code. It will match all code that has the same syntactical structure. You can use `$` sign + upper case letters as a [wildcard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wildcard_character), e.g. `$MATCH`, to match any single AST node. Think of it as [regular expression dot](https://regexone.com/lesson/wildcards_dot) `.`, except it is not textual. Try the [online playground](https://ast-grep.github.io/playground.html) for a taste! ## Screenshot ![demo](https://ast-grep.github.io/image/search-replace.png) See more screenshots on the [website](https://ast-grep.github.io/). ## Installation You can install ast-grep from npm, pip, cargo, cargo-binstall, homebrew, scoop, mise, or MacPorts: ```bash npm install --global @ast-grep/cli # `pnpm approve-builds` may be needed pip install ast-grep-cli brew install ast-grep cargo install ast-grep --locked cargo binstall ast-grep # install via scoop scoop install main/ast-grep # install via MacPorts sudo port install ast-grep # try ast-grep in nix-shell nix-shell -p ast-grep # try ast-grep with mise mise use -g ast-grep ``` [Packages](https://repology.org/project/ast-grep/versions) are available on other platforms too. ## Command line usage ast-grep has the following form: ```bash ast-grep --pattern 'var code = $PATTERN' --rewrite 'let code = new $PATTERN' --lang ts ``` ### Examples * Rewrite code using null coalescing operator: ```bash ast-grep -p '$A && $A()' -l ts -r '$A?.()' ``` * Rewrite Zodios code: ```bash ast-grep -p 'new Zodios($URL, $CONF as const,)' -l ts -r 'new Zodios($URL, $CONF)' -i ``` ## Features ast-grep helps you search and replace code based on abstract syntax trees. It can help you do lightweight static analysis and massive scale code manipulation in an intuitive way.                 if bl.strip():
                    bi = len(bl) - len(bl.lstrip(" "))
                    if bi <= indent:
                        break
                    min_indent = bi if min_indent is None else min(min_indent, bi)
                    block.append(bl)
                else:
                    block.append("")
                i += 1
            mi = min_indent or (indent + 2)
            cleaned = []
            for b in block:
                if b:
                    cleaned.append(b[mi:] if len(b) >= mi else "")
                else:
                    cleaned.append("")
            content = f"{key}: " + json.dumps("\n".join(cleaned))
            out.append((indent, content))
            continue
        out.append((indent, content.strip()))
        i += 1
    return out


def parse_yaml_text(text: str) -> Any:
    lines = prepare_yaml_lines(text)
    if not lines:
        return None

    def parse_block(idx: int, indent: int) -> Tuple[Any, int]:
        if idx >= len(lines):
            return None, idx
        if lines[idx][0] < indent:
            return None, idx
        is_list = lines[idx][1].startswith("- ") or lines[idx][1] == "-"
        if is_list:
            arr: List[Any] = []
            while idx < len(lines) and lines[idx][0] == indent and (lines[idx][1].startswith("- ") or lines[idx][1] == "-"):
                rest = lines[idx][1][1:].strip()
                idx += 1
                if not rest:
                    if idx < len(lines) and lines[idx][0] > indent:
                        val, idx = parse_block(idx, lines[idx][0])
                    else:
                        val = None
                    arr.append(val)
                else:
                    k, v = split_key_value(rest)
                    if v is not None:
                        item: Dict[str, Any] = {k: parse_scalar(v) if v != "" else None}
                        if v == "" and idx < len(lines) and lines[idx][0] > indent:
                            child, idx = parse_block(idx, lines[idx][0])
                            item[k] = child
                        if idx < len(lines) and lines[idx][0] > indent:
                            child, idx = parse_block(idx, lines[idx][0])
                            if isinstance(child, dict):
                                item.update(child)
                        arr.append(item)
                    else:
                        arr.append(parse_scalar(rest))
            return arr, idx
        mp: Dict[str, Any] = {}
        while idx < len(lines) and lines[idx][0] == indent and not (lines[idx][1].startswith("- ") or lines[idx][1] == "-"):
            content = lines[idx][1]
            key, val = split_key_value(content)
            idx += 1
            if val is None:
                mp[key] = None
            elif val == "":
                if idx < len(lines) and lines[idx][0] > indent:
                    child, idx = parse_block(idx, lines[idx][0])
                    mp[key] = child
                else:
                    mp[key] = None
            else:
                mp[key] = parse_scalar(val)
        return mp, idx

    result, _ = parse_block(0, lines[0][0])
    return result

def lang_from_arg(s: Optional[str]) -> Optional[str]:
    if s is None:
        return None
    k = s.lower()
    if k in SUPPORTED_LANGS:
        return SUPPORTED_LANGS[k][0]
    # Accept canonical spelling case-insensitively.
    for canon in CANONICAL_EXTS:
        if k == canon.lower():
            return canon
    return None


def lang_for_path(path: str) -> Optional[str]:
    lower = path.lower()
    # tsx before ts, c++ headers are ambiguous but good enough.
    for canon, exts in CANONICAL_EXTS.items():
        for ext in sorted(exts, key=len, reverse=True):
            if lower.endswith(ext):
                return canon
    return None

def line_col(text: str, pos: int) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    pos = max(0, min(pos, len(text)))
    line = text.count("\n", 0, pos)
    last = text.rfind("\n", 0, pos)
    col = pos if last < 0 else pos - last - 1
    return line, col


def line_bounds(text: str, line: int) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    starts = [0]
    for i, ch in enumerate(text):
        if ch == "\n":
            starts.append(i + 1)
    if line < 0:
        line = 0
    if line >= len(starts):
        return len(text), len(text)
    start = starts[line]
    end = text.find("\n", start)
    if end < 0:
        end = len(text)
    return start, end


def get_lines_for_range(text: str, start: int, end: int) -> str:
    sl, _ = line_col(text, start)
    el, ec = line_col(text, end)
    if end > start and ec == 0 and el > sl:
        el -= 1
    s, _ = line_bounds(text, sl)
    _, e = line_bounds(text, el)
    return text[s:e]


def match_to_json(m: Match, include_rule: bool = False) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    text = m.source.text
    sl, sc = line_col(text, m.start)
    el, ec = line_col(text, m.end)
    lines = get_lines_for_range(text, m.start, m.end)
    last_line = lines.split("\n")[-1] if lines else ""
    obj: Dict[str, Any] = {
        "text": m.text,
        "range": {
            "byteOffset": {"start": m.start, "end": m.end},
            "start": {"line": sl, "column": sc},
            "end": {"line": el, "column": ec},
        },
        "file": m.file,
        "lines": lines,
        "charCount": {"leading": sc, "trailing": max(0, len(last_line) - ec) if sl == el else max(0, len(last_line) - ec)},
    }
    if m.replacement is not None:
        obj["replacement"] = m.replacement
        obj["replacementOffsets"] = {"start": m.replacement_start if m.replacement_start is not None else m.start,
                                      "end": m.replacement_end if m.replacement_end is not None else m.end}
    obj["language"] = display_lang(m.source.language)
    if m.captures or m.multi:
        single: Dict[str, Any] = {}
        for name, (val, s, e) in m.captures.items():
            l1, c1 = line_col(text, s); l2, c2 = line_col(text, e)
            single[name] = {"text": val, "range": {"byteOffset": {"start": s, "end": e},
                                                     "start": {"line": l1, "column": c1},
                                                     "end": {"line": l2, "column": c2}}}
        multi: Dict[str, Any] = {}
        for name, vals in m.multi.items():
            arr = []
            for val, s, e in vals:
                l1, c1 = line_col(text, s); l2, c2 = line_col(text, e)
                arr.append({"text": val, "range": {"byteOffset": {"start": s, "end": e},
                                                     "start": {"line": l1, "column": c1},
                                                     "end": {"line": l2, "column": c2}}})
            multi[name] = arr
        obj["metaVariables"] = {"single": single, "multi": multi, "transformed": {}}
    if include_rule or m.rule_id:
        obj["ruleId"] = m.rule_id
        obj["severity"] = m.severity
        obj["note"] = m.note
        obj["message"] = m.message
        obj["labels"] = [{"text": m.text, "range": obj["range"], "style": "primary"}]
    return obj

def strip_comment(line: str) -> str:
    in_s = in_d = False
    esc = False
    for i, ch in enumerate(line):
        if esc:
            esc = False
            continue
        if ch == "\\" and in_d:
            esc = True

        if ch == "'" and not in_d:

def parse_scalar(s: str) -> Any:
    s = s.strip()
    if s == "":
        return ""
    low = s.lower()
    if low in ("null", "~"):
        return None
    if low == "true":
        return True
    if low == "false":
        return False
    if s.startswith('"') and s.endswith('"') and len(s) >= 2:
        try:
            return bytes(s[1:-1], "utf-8").decode("unicode_escape")
        except Exception:
            return s[1:-1]
    if s.startswith("'") and s.endswith("'") and len(s) >= 2:
        return s[1:-1].replace("''", "'")
    if s.startswith("[") and s.endswith("]"):
        inner = s[1:-1].strip()
        if not inner:
            return []
        parts: List[str] = []
        cur = ""
        depth = 0
        in_s = in_d = False
        for ch in inner:
            if ch == "'" and not in_d:
                in_s = not in_s
            elif ch == '"' and not in_s:
                in_d = not in_d
            elif ch in "[{" and not in_s and not in_d:
                depth += 1
            elif ch in "]}" and not in_s and not in_d:
                depth -= 1
            if ch == "," and depth == 0 and not in_s and not in_d:
                parts.append(cur.strip()); cur = ""
            else:
                cur += ch
        if cur.strip():
            parts.append(cur.strip())
        return [parse_scalar(p) for p in parts]
    if re.fullmatch(r"-?\d+", s):
        try:
            return int(s)
        except Exception:
            pass
    return s

def prepare_yaml_lines(text: str) -> List[Tuple[int, str]]:
    raw = text.splitlines()
    out: List[Tuple[int, str]] = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(raw):
        line = raw[i].replace("\t", "    ")
        if not line.strip():
            i += 1; continue
        indent = len(line) - len(line.lstrip(" "))
        content = strip_comment(line[indent:])
        if not content.strip():
            i += 1; continue
        key, val = split_key_value(content)
        if val is not None and val in ("|", "|-", "|+", ">", ">-", ">+"):
            block: List[str] = []
            i += 1
            min_indent: Optional[int] = None
            while i < len(raw):
                bl = raw[i].replace("\t", "    ")
                if bl.strip():
                    bi = len(bl) - len(bl.lstrip(" "))
                    if bi <= indent:
                        break
                    min_indent = bi if min_indent is None else min(min_indent, bi)
                    block.append(bl)
                else:
                    block.append("")
                i += 1
            mi = min_indent or (indent + 2)
            cleaned = []
            for b in block:
                if b:
                    cleaned.append(b[mi:] if len(b) >= mi else "")
                else:
                    cleaned.append("")
            content = f"{key}: " + json.dumps("\n".join(cleaned))
            out.append((indent, content))
            continue
        out.append((indent, content.strip()))
        i += 1
    return out


def parse_yaml_text(text: str) -> Any:
    lines = prepare_yaml_lines(text)
    if not lines:
        return None

    def parse_block(idx: int, indent: int) -> Tuple[Any, int]:
        if idx >= len(lines):
            return None, idx
        if lines[idx][0] < indent:
            return None, idx
        is_list = lines[idx][1].startswith("- ") or lines[idx][1] == "-"
        if is_list:
            arr: List[Any] = []
            while idx < len(lines) and lines[idx][0] == indent and (lines[idx][1].startswith("- ") or lines[idx][1] == "-"):
                rest = lines[idx][1][1:].strip()
                idx += 1
                if not rest:
                    if idx < len(lines) and lines[idx][0] > indent:
                        val, idx = parse_block(idx, lines[idx][0])
                    else:
                        val = None
                    arr.append(val)
                else:
                    k, v = split_key_value(rest)
                    if v is not None:
                        item: Dict[str, Any] = {k: parse_scalar(v) if v != "" else None}
                        if v == "" and idx < len(lines) and lines[idx][0] > indent:
                            child, idx = parse_block(idx, lines[idx][0])
                            item[k] = child
                        if idx < len(lines) and lines[idx][0] > indent:
                            child, idx = parse_block(idx, lines[idx][0])
                            if isinstance(child, dict):
                                item.update(child)
                        arr.append(item)
                    else:
                        arr.append(parse_scalar(rest))
            return arr, idx
        mp: Dict[str, Any] = {}
        while idx < len(lines) and lines[idx][0] == indent and not (lines[idx][1].startswith("- ") or lines[idx][1] == "-"):
            content = lines[idx][1]
            key, val = split_key_value(content)
            idx += 1
            if val is None:
                mp[key] = None
            elif val == "":
                if idx < len(lines) and lines[idx][0] > indent:
                    child, idx = parse_block(idx, lines[idx][0])
                    mp[key] = child
                else:
                    mp[key] = None
            else:
                mp[key] = parse_scalar(val)

    result, _ = parse_block(0, lines[0][0])

@dataclass
class FileSource:
    path: str
    text: str
    language: str

    def line_starts(self) -> List[int]:
        starts = [0]
        for i, ch in enumerate(self.text):
            if ch == "\n":
                starts.append(i + 1)

@dataclass
class Match:
    file: str
    source: FileSource
    start: int
    end: int
    captures: Dict[str, Tuple[str, int, int]] = field(default_factory=dict)
    multi: Dict[str, List[Tuple[str, int, int]]] = field(default_factory=dict)

    replacement_start: Optional[int] = None
    replacement_end: Optional[int] = None

    severity: Optional[str] = None
    message: Optional[str] = None
    note: Optional[str] = None

    @property

def lang_from_arg(s: Optional[str]) -> Optional[str]:
    if s is None:
        return None
    k = s.lower()
    if k in SUPPORTED_LANGS:
        return SUPPORTED_LANGS[k][0]
    # Accept canonical spelling case-insensitively.
    for canon in CANONICAL_EXTS:
        if k == canon.lower():
            return canon
    return None


def lang_for_path(path: str) -> Optional[str]:
    lower = path.lower()
    # tsx before ts, c++ headers are ambiguous but good enough.
    for canon, exts in CANONICAL_EXTS.items():
        for ext in sorted(exts, key=len, reverse=True):
            if lower.endswith(ext):
                return canon
    return None


def display_lang(canon: Optional[str]) -> str:
    return canon or "Unknown"


def rel_path(path: Path) -> str:
    try:
        return path.relative_to(Path.cwd()).as_posix()
    except Exception:
        return path.as_posix()


def line_col(text: str, pos: int) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    pos = max(0, min(pos, len(text)))
    line = text.count("\n", 0, pos)
    last = text.rfind("\n", 0, pos)
    col = pos if last < 0 else pos - last - 1
    return line, col


def line_bounds(text: str, line: int) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    starts = [0]
    for i, ch in enumerate(text):
        if ch == "\n":
            starts.append(i + 1)
    if line < 0:
        line = 0
    if line >= len(starts):
        return len(text), len(text)
    start = starts[line]
    end = text.find("\n", start)
    if end < 0:
        end = len(text)
    return start, end


def get_lines_for_range(text: str, start: int, end: int) -> str:
    sl, _ = line_col(text, start)
    el, ec = line_col(text, end)
    if end > start and ec == 0 and el > sl:
        el -= 1
    s, _ = line_bounds(text, sl)
    _, e = line_bounds(text, el)
    return text[s:e]


def match_to_json(m: Match, include_rule: bool = False) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    text = m.source.text
    sl, sc = line_col(text, m.start)
    el, ec = line_col(text, m.end)
    lines = get_lines_for_range(text, m.start, m.end)
    last_line = lines.split("\n")[-1] if lines else ""
    obj: Dict[str, Any] = {
        "text": m.text,
        "range": {
            "byteOffset": {"start": m.start, "end": m.end},
            "start": {"line": sl, "column": sc},
            "end": {"line": el, "column": ec},
        },
        "file": m.file,
        "lines": lines,
        "charCount": {"leading": sc, "trailing": max(0, len(last_line) - ec) if sl == el else max(0, len(last_line) - ec)},
    }
    if m.replacement is not None:
        obj["replacement"] = m.replacement
        obj["replacementOffsets"] = {"start": m.replacement_start if m.replacement_start is not None else m.start,
                                      "end": m.replacement_end if m.replacement_end is not None else m.end}
    obj["language"] = display_lang(m.source.language)
    if m.captures or m.multi:
        single: Dict[str, Any] = {}
        for name, (val, s, e) in m.captures.items():
            l1, c1 = line_col(text, s); l2, c2 = line_col(text, e)
            single[name] = {"text": val, "range": {"byteOffset": {"start": s, "end": e},
                                                     "start": {"line": l1, "column": c1},
                                                     "end": {"line": l2, "column": c2}}}
        multi: Dict[str, Any] = {}
        for name, vals in m.multi.items():
            arr = []
            for val, s, e in vals:
                l1, c1 = line_col(text, s); l2, c2 = line_col(text, e)
                arr.append({"text": val, "range": {"byteOffset": {"start": s, "end": e},
                                                     "start": {"line": l1, "column": c1},
                                                     "end": {"line": l2, "column": c2}}})
            multi[name] = arr
        obj["metaVariables"] = {"single": single, "multi": multi, "transformed": {}}
    if include_rule or m.rule_id:
        obj["ruleId"] = m.rule_id
        obj["severity"] = m.severity
        obj["note"] = m.note
        obj["message"] = m.message
        obj["labels"] = [{"text": m.text, "range": obj["range"], "style": "primary"}]
    return obj

    if not objs:
        return "[]"
    parts = [json.dumps(o, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) for o in objs]
    return "[\n" + ",\n".join(parts) + "\n]"
